info.title: Neosian storage HTTP contract
info.description: Storage wire 6, independent of package version. Bodies are JSON objects regardless of Content-Type; legacy operations ignore unknown request keys and treat optional null as absence. Optional memory-search version 1 uses strict fields and types, with null allowed only for cursor. JSON Schema describes supported typed input, not legacy coercions. Scope/conversation allowances are literal prefixes; constrained tokens cannot call store/* or /mcp and must explicitly bound conversation searches/trail reads. MCP at /mcp is a separate negotiated protocol, not described by this document.

authorization.description: Optional opt-in grant enforcement capability, versioned separately from wire 6. Required by portable HTTP profiles.

memory_search.description: Optional current-memory lexical search contract version 1. Its absence means memory/search is unsupported.

post.summary: Search current memory in one authorized scope (optional version 1)

query.description: 1..16 whitespace terms, all matched as per-scalar Unicode-17.0.0 per-scalar lowercase substrings across selected values. No stemming, normalization or regex.

prefix.description: Case-sensitive literal document-path prefix, at most 1024 UTF-8 bytes.

cursor.description: Opaque keyset continuation bound to scope, query, prefix, fields and metadata keys. Not a permission token or snapshot.

schema.description: Requires memory_search version 1. Unknown fields and mistyped/default-null fields refuse. metadata requires 1..8 metadata_keys; keys require the metadata field. Scope authorization precedes scanning and pagination.

excerpt.description: Up to 240 original Unicode scalars, starting up to 40 scalars before the first match. Offset is zero-based within the path, body or matched metadata string value. Content is preferred, then selected metadata keys, then path.

schema.description: Ascending document-path order. A nonfinal page has exactly limit hits; no total count. Only current, non-redacted memory documents are searched. sessions/, messages/, message-links/ and handoff are excluded. Each page reads current state; writes before the last key require a new query.
